summary: New sense 2: (Detrans.) sich an einen Ort begeben, einen Ort aufsuchen

data.gloss: (Detrans.) sich an einen Ort begeben, einen Ort aufsuchen

rationale: qṣido with feminine pilgrim subject and harke is visitor motion, not needing assistance and not being sought. One attestation supports a provisional distinct Detransitive use. Existing unnumbered Detransitive need/help material is left in its inherited position, reserving index 1.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (69/537)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Lo! Aṯiwa ḥḏo ḥaǧǧiye, azəlto lu ḥaǧ w qṣido (+det) harke, səmlila fako d muklo, xila w azzala."
data.translation: "Nein! Es ist nur eine Pilgersfrau gekommen, auf dem Wege zur Wallfahrt. Die ist zufällig hierher geraten. Da habe ich ihr einen Bissen zu essen zurechtgemacht, den hat sie gegessen und ist dann fortgegangen."

rationale: One clear Detransitive visitor-motion attestation with feminine subject and local adverb. German zufällig is copied as edition wording but excluded from the sense gloss.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (115/304)

data.turoyo: Rawəx ʕal u səsyayḏe w yalla səmle, qṣədle i hno, i škafte, <...>
data.translation: Er bestieg sein Pferd und los! Er suchte die Höhle auf, <...>

rationale: Second actual Preterit context for sense 1: zero-marked cave goal. The inherited example lists 115/304 only as a secondary reference, not this text.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.10/2522)

data.turoyo: <...> Əno qṣədli aġ ġayri-musləm dəṯxu, ann armənoye, d kətne bi qriṯo. <...>
data.translation: <...> I meant your non-Muslims, the Armenians who are in the village. <...>

rationale: Thin active I.1 Preterit: explicit intended referent supplies the meaning half absent from the existing travel examples.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/121)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Baš šəbqono i naqla d kəmmina u lišonayḏan w dowina moro lu lišonayḏan, l ġalabe ma mfarǧonayḏan, u lišono w aḥ ḥarfe, baḥ ḥarfat səryoye koquṣdi.
data.translation: Atiya Xamri: But excuse me, when we say our language and take care of our language, for many of our viewers, the language and the letters, they mean the Syriac letters.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum: third-plural form and baḥ ḥarfat term clarify linguistic reference; preserve machine person wording.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/220)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Mən koquṣdat bi šuqo?
data.translation: Atiya Xamri: What do you mean by market?

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum with an overt b-marked expression whose meaning is queried.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/852)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya: Kuḏʕət i naqla d kəmmono i ʕito, kquṣdono ste i ṣəʕṯo di ʕito, kul mede d kətle ʕalaqa bi ʕitayḏan.
data.translation: Atiya: You know, when I say the church, I also mean the church board, everything that has a connection with our church.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum: first-singular kquṣdono with church/body referent clarifies reference beyond word definitions.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/861)

data.turoyo: Maydina, koquṣdina, maydina b Orabro (Örebro) fahimat? Səmme yaʕni, d əbʕat, fayəš mən d əmmat ste, kəbʕi d saymi qaše ġalabe, hano ṭowo yo lu ʕəlmayḏan.
data.translation: Let us take, we mean, let us take Örebro, do you understand? They have done, that is, if you want, it remains whatever you say too; they want to make many priests, this is good for our people.

rationale: Completes I.1 Infectum to five; first-plural koquṣdina appears within an explicit reference repair.

summary: Active I.1 already combines intending and seeking a destination. Both textual active occurrences support its aufsuchen component; no split or renumbering is justified. The new Detransitive use has a mobile subject and local adverb, without an agent causing it to be sought.

Existing I Detransitive boxes have four unnumbered need/help examples and no separate parsed sense list. Their order and wording are preserved, with index 1 reserved; new motion use is appended as 2. Stem II Detransitive mqaṣəd is already a separate entry section and is not confused with qṣido.

115/304 supplies a cave destination, whereas the printed example text is the tailor’s shop from 52/179. Treat the extra reference as parallel sense evidence, without claiming an erroneous citation. The omitted final relative clause has u muklo but edition Wasser; no translation correction is invented.
Jan's English is project machine translation, copied only as supplied and not used to establish senses. All interpretations were checked against the Turoyo.
All Jan occurrences are active I.1 mean/intend, not the round-1 Detransitive visitor use. No new sense or stem is needed.

Koquṣdi, kquṣdono and koquṣdina provide third-plural, first-singular and first-plural surface contrasts; retain source vocalism. The qsd send entry mentioned by a reader is distinct and causes no entry correction.
69/537: confirm qṣido as I Detransitive Preterit, rather than a result-state adjective, and the goal value of harke. Is this visitor-motion use conventional? Only one token is available.

Confirm formal numbering of the unnumbered I Detransitive need/help material before editorial adoption of appended sense 2. 115/304: check edition Wasser against source u muklo; the mismatching clause is excluded from the added excerpt.
Confirm first-singular versus plural person in Jan 4.I/121 against koquṣdi; the machine English is not morphological evidence.
Should the b-marked quoted term in Jan 4.I/220 receive an explicit government note under I.1? The meaning remains mean/intend.
Check whether 115/304 is a supplementary attestation

data.question: Is 115/304 intentionally a supplementary verb attestation rather than a source of the quoted sentence?

rationale: The quoted journey to the tailor’s shop matches the supplied 52/179. At 115/304 the same verb qṣədle occurs, but he seeks a cave instead. This may be an intentional supplementary attestation; the evidence does not justify replacing or deleting it automatically.

summary: English typo: “wil” → “will”
before: The day I wil need you
after: The day I will need you
rationale: The English auxiliary “will” is misspelled with one l.

summary: Intended referents include people, letters, an institution and an aim. B- can mark the term being explained; this specializes the inherited mean/intend meaning without a separate sense.
